vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on SetFeeValue Allows Fee Manipulation
vulnerabilities.description: The set_fee_value function lacks access control on the fee update operation, allowing any caller to set the protocol fee to 0%.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in `transfer_nft` and `_transfer_nft`
vulnerabilities.description: The `transfer_nft` and `_transfer_nft` functions allow token transfers without requiring users to specify minimum acceptable outputs, exposing them to unfavorable execution when execution differs from requests.

vulnerabilities.title: Validation Timing in `setlistforsell`
vulnerabilities.description: The `setlistforsell` function validates parameters after state changes, allowing invalid operations to complete.

vulnerabilities.title: Execution Boundaries and Validation Consistency in `transfer_nft`
vulnerabilities.description: The `transfer_nft` function executes differently than initially requested without maintaining consistency between expected and actual execution.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Critical State Modification Functions
vulnerabilities.description: The contract exposes multiple functions that modify critical state without access control modifiers. Specifically, `set_fee()`, `increase_balance()`, `decrease_balance()`, `increment_tokens()`, and `decrement_tokens()` all modify state variables that affect economic calculations (fees, balances, token counts) without any access restrictions.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in Balance Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The increase_balance and decrease_balance functions modify user asset values without providing mechanisms for users to express acceptable execution bounds. This exposes users to unfavorable execution outcomes when operations can be partially executed.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Missing User Control Over Execution Outcomes

vulnerabilities.title: Validation Timing Vulnerability in Balance Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The increase_balance and decrease_balance functions modify state (balance updates) before validation is complete. The functions load the current balance, modify it, and save it back. If the save operation fails after the modification, the balance is left in an inconsistent state.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Fee Management Functions
vulnerabilities.description: The set_fee function allows any user to modify the protocol fee without access control restrictions. This is a critical vulnerability as it allows malicious actors to set arbitrary fees, potentially draining the protocol or causing economic damage.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Fee Update Function
vulnerabilities.description: The `set_fee` function allows any caller to update the protocol fee without access control. This enables attackers to manipulate fee calculations by setting fees to zero or negative values before critical operations like fee collection or distribution.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Token URI Validation and Initialization
vulnerabilities.description: The TokenInfo struct has an optional token_uri field, but there is no validation or initialization logic for this field. This can lead to undefined behavior when the token_uri is accessed without proper initialization or validation.

vulnerabilities.title: Inadequate Approval Expiration Handling
vulnerabilities.description: The Approval struct has an expiration field, but the is_expired method only checks if the expiration is expired without handling the case where the approval is not expired but the token is no longer valid.
vulnerabilities.location: Approval struct and is_expired method, line ~250-260

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Balance Validation in Balance Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The decrease_balance function does not validate that the balance is sufficient before decreasing it. This can lead to underflow and unexpected behavior.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Token Count Validation
vulnerabilities.description: The decrement_tokens function does not validate that the token count is greater than zero before decrementing it. This can lead to underflow and unexpected behavior.

vulnerabilities.title: Authorization Context Binding Vulnerability in Rental Approval Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The contract implements rental approval operations (e.g., setapproveforshortterm, setapproveforlongterm) that do not bind the execution context to the authorization signature. This allows front-runners to submit the same authorization with hostile execution contexts, consuming the authorization while executing in a different context than intended.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Caller Verification in Default Currency Handler Triggers Unintended Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Contract struct defines a balances Map but lacks any explicit default currency handler (fallback/receive) for receiving native tokens. When native tokens are sent to the contract, they accumulate in the contract's balance without any verification of caller identity or transaction origin. This allows any external actor to send tokens to the contract, potentially interfering with withdrawal flows or deposit accounting.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Missing Caller Verification in Automatic Handler

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Critical Execute Functions
vulnerabilities.description: The ExecuteMsg enum defines multiple functions that modify state or transfer value without access control. Critical functions like Mint, Withdraw, SetFeeValue, SetListForSell, SetBidToBuy, SetListForShortTermRental, SetReservationForShortTerm, CancelReservationForShortterm, CancelRentalForShortterm, RejectReservationForShortterm, SetApproveForShortTerm, FinalizeShortTermRental, WithdrawToLandlord, SetListForLongTermRental, SetReservationForLongTerm, RejectReservationForLongterm, CancelReservationForLongterm, CancelRentalForLongterm, DepositForLongTermRental, SetApproveForLongTerm, FinalizeLongTermRental, and Extension (for E) lack access control. This allows any actor to mint NFTs, withdraw funds, modify fees, list items for sale, make reservations, finalize rentals, and execute arbitrary extension messages.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Input Validation on Execution Parameters
vulnerabilities.description: The ExecuteMsg enum defines functions that accept parameters that should be validated but lack validation. Functions like SetListForSell, SetBidToBuy, SetListForShortTermRental, SetReservationForShortTerm, CancelReservationForShortterm, CancelRentalForShortterm, RejectReservationForShortterm, SetApproveForShortTerm, FinalizeShortTermRental, WithdrawToLandlord, SetListForLongTermRental, SetReservationForLongTerm, RejectReservationForLongterm, CancelReservationForLongterm, CancelRentalForLongterm, DepositForLongTermRental, SetApproveForLongTerm, FinalizeLongTermRental, and Extension (for E) accept parameters that should be validated but lack validation. This allows invalid parameters to be passed to execution functions, potentially causing incorrect behavior.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing State Synchronization in Rental Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The ExecuteMsg enum defines rental-related functions (SetListForShortTermRental, SetReservationForShortTerm, CancelReservationForShortterm, CancelRentalForShortterm, RejectReservationForShortterm, SetApproveForShortTerm, FinalizeShortTermRental, WithdrawToLandlord, SetListForLongTermRental, SetReservationForLongTerm, RejectReservationForLongterm, CancelReservationForLongterm, CancelRentalForLongterm, DepositForLongTermRental, SetApproveForLongTerm, FinalizeLongTermRental) that modify state but lack synchronization between related state variables. When these functions update state, they may cause state desynchronization between related variables, leading to incorrect accounting and potential loss of funds.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Mathematical Precision in Fee Calculations
vulnerabilities.description: The ExecuteMsg enum defines functions that perform calculations (SetFeeValue, SetListForSell, SetBidToBuy, SetListForShortTermRental, SetReservationForShortTerm, CancelReservationForShortterm, CancelRentalForShortterm, RejectReservationForShortterm, SetApproveForShortTerm, FinalizeShortTermRental, WithdrawToLandlord, SetListForLongTermRental, SetReservationForLongTerm, RejectReservationForLongterm, CancelReservationForLongterm, CancelRentalForLongterm, DepositForLongTermRental, SetApproveForLongTerm, FinalizeLongTermRental) that may involve division operations that could round to zero. This can cause incorrect fee calculations and accounting errors.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Withdrawal Destination Verification in Withdrawal Function
vulnerabilities.description: The ExecuteMsg::Withdraw variant allows any caller to specify an arbitrary target address and amount to withdraw native tokens. There is no verification that the caller has a valid claim to the specified amount or that the target address is authorized to receive funds. This enables unauthorized fund extraction by specifying arbitrary target addresses.

vulnerabilities.title: Authorization Context Binding Missing in Signature-Based Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The ExecuteMsg enum defines several rental-related messages (e.g., Approve, ApproveAll, SetApproveForShortTermRental, SetApproveForLongTermRental) that appear to be signature-based authorization operations, but the message structure does not bind the intended executor or execution context. This allows anyone who obtains a valid authorization message to execute it in a different context, enabling front-running and unauthorized execution.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in Mint/Burn Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The contract's Mint and Burn operations do not provide users with mechanisms to specify minimum acceptable outputs or execution bounds. When users request token minting or burning, they cannot protect themselves against unfavorable execution conditions. This exposes users to potential loss of funds if execution is incomplete or partial.

vulnerabilities.title: Validation Timing Issue in Mint Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The Mint operation validates parameters after state changes instead of before. The function executes the mint operation first, then validates parameters. This allows invalid operations to complete successfully, leading to protocol instability and potential fund loss.

vulnerabilities.title: Access Control Issue in Interface
vulnerabilities.description: The interface declares critical functions without access control indicators. Functions like pool creation, fee collection, parameter changes should indicate restrictions but do not. This is a vulnerability because interfaces should reflect security expectations for critical functions.

vulnerabilities.title: State Synchronization Issue in Function Chains
vulnerabilities.description: When functions call other internal functions, state is updated before the dependent call. This creates a synchronization issue where dependent functions may use stale state values, leading to incorrect calculations and potential fund loss.

vulnerabilities.title: Return Value Unit Consistency Issue
vulnerabilities.description: When functions implement interfaces or override base functions, return values do not use expected units. This creates unit mismatches that cause incorrect calculations and accounting errors, potentially leading to fund loss.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Context Binding in Ownership Transfer
vulnerabilities.description: The contract implements ownership transfer via cw_ownable::Action::TransferOwnership with a pending_owner and pending_expiry, but the authorization digest does not bind the intended executor (submitter). This allows front-runners to consume the pending ownership transfer with hostile context, causing the nonce/pending state to be consumed while the intended transfer fails.

vulnerabilities.title: Critical: Missing User Protection in Withdraw Functions Allows Unauthorized Fund Extraction

This violates Pattern 1 (Missing User Protection) and Pattern 7 (State Commitment Timing) as funds can be withdrawn without user protection against manipulation or partial execution failures.

This allows invalid operations to complete, as validation occurs after token transfers, balance updates, or swap execution. Since validation timing is incorrect, invalid operations can complete, leading to fund loss.

vulnerabilities.title: High: Access Control Issues in ExecuteMsg Interface
vulnerabilities.description: The ExecuteMsg interface declares critical functions (Withdraw, WithdrawToLandlord) without access control indicators (Pattern 4). This is a vulnerability as interface design should reflect security expectations. Critical functions should indicate restrictions, but the interface shows no access control expectations for these functions.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Access Control Issues in ExecuteMsg Interface

vulnerabilities.title: High: State Synchronization Issues in Function Chains
vulnerabilities.description: The Withdraw and WithdrawToLandlord functions likely call other internal functions, and state may be updated before the dependent call (Pattern 6). This is a vulnerability as state modifications may happen before the dependent function executes. When operations reduce state values and trigger dependent operations, state may be set to final intended value before dependent function reads it. If dependent function reads state before reset, it may use stale state value.

However, since this is an error definition file, the vulnerability assessment must consider that if any functions in the broader contract (not shown) modify state variables used in economic calculations (e.g., deposits, rental amounts, approvals, balances), and those functions lack access control, users could manipulate timing or values before admin operations.
vulnerabilities.location: N/A - no functions defined in this file

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Domain Validation in Mathematical Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The code lacks validation for mathematical domain constraints, particularly for logarithmic and square root operations. When invalid inputs (zero, negative values) are silently accepted, the operations produce mathematically impossible results without error.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Context Binding in Signature-Based Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The ContractError enum defines authorization-related errors like 'Ownership', 'ApprovedAlready', 'AlreadyReserved', 'NotApproved', 'NotListed', 'RentalActive', 'RentalAlreadyStarted', 'RentalNotActivated', 'UnavailablePeriod', 'InvalidInput', 'LessThanMinimum', 'Expired', 'RefundableAmount', and 'ApprovalNotFound'. However, none of these errors bind the authorization context (e.g., caller address, execution parameters) to the authorization signature or approval. This allows front-running attacks where an attacker can capture a valid authorization and replay it with hostile context (e.g., different recipient, amount, or parameters). The vulnerability is in the design of the error system itself, which lacks any authorization binding mechanism.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on State-Modifying Functions
vulnerabilities.description: The file defines query message types but no actual query handler functions. However, the cw721 standard requires state management functions (e.g., transfer, approve, setApprovalForAll, etc.) are missing entirely. Without proper access control on state-modifying functions, any actor can manipulate token ownership, approvals, and operator permissions, leading to complete protocol compromise.
vulnerabilities.location: N/A - No query handler functions present

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in Withdrawal/Refund Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The ContractError enum defines a RefundableAmount error variant that includes an amount field: `RefundableAmount { amount: String }`. This indicates the contract has logic to calculate refundable amounts, but there is no corresponding function that implements the actual refund operation. Without a properly implemented refund function with user-controlled minimum acceptable output parameters, users cannot protect against manipulation of refund calculations.

vulnerabilities.title: Inconsistent State Management for Refund Calculations
vulnerabilities.description: The ContractError enum includes both `RefundableAmount { amount: String }` and `ApprovalNotFound { spender: String }` variants. This suggests the contract has logic to track refundable amounts and approval states, but there is no corresponding function that implements the actual refund operation. Without a properly implemented refund function with user-controlled minimum acceptable output parameters, users cannot protect against manipulation of refund calculations.
vulnerabilities.location: ContractError::RefundableAmount { amount: String } and ContractError::ApprovalNotFound { spender: String }

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Critical Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The ContractError enum includes `InsufficientDeposit {}`, `UnavailableAmount {}`, and `RefundableAmount { amount: String }` variants. This indicates the contract has logic to handle deposit amounts and refund calculations, but there is no corresponding function that implements the actual refund operation. Without a properly implemented refund function with user-controlled minimum acceptable output parameters, users cannot protect against manipulation of refund calculations.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on State-Modifying Functions in Query Module
vulnerabilities.description: The file cw721/src/query.rs defines numerous query-related data structures (e.g., Cw721QueryMsg variants, response structs like OwnerOfResponse, Approval, etc.), but it contains no functions that modify state. However, in a typical CW721 implementation, functions like `owner_of`, `approval`, `operator`, etc., would be implemented elsewhere (e.g., in execute.rs or contract.rs). If the corresponding execute functions (e.g., `update_owner`, `set_approval`, `remove_approval`, etc.) exist and modify state variables used in economic calculations (e.g., balances, deposits, fees, rental periods, cancellation terms), they must have proper access control. Without access control, attackers could manipulate state before admin operations, affecting fee calculations, deposit amounts, rental periods, and other economic parameters.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Input Validation in Query Messages
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw7221QueryMsg enum defines query messages but lacks validation for critical fields like token_id, owner, and spender addresses. This allows malformed inputs that could cause unexpected behavior in query execution.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Execute Traits Allows Unauthorized State Modification
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Execute trait defines multiple execute functions (transfer_nft, send_nft, approve, revoke, burn, etc.) without any access control modifiers. These functions modify critical state such as token ownership, approvals, and balances. Without access control, any actor can call these functions, enabling unauthorized transfers, approvals, and destruction of NFTs.
vulnerabilities.location: Lines 37-102, especially transfer_nft (line 40), send_nft (line 47), approve (line 55), revoke (line 63), burn (line 87)

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Context Binding in Cw721QueryMsg
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721QueryMsg enum defines query messages for a CW721 (CosmWasm NFT) implementation, but lacks any authorization context binding. This means that any actor can construct valid query messages for arbitrary token IDs and owner addresses without cryptographic binding to the intended requester. This enables front-running attacks where malicious actors can construct queries that appear legitimate but are actually unauthorized access attempts.

vulnerabilities.title: Type Representation Ambiguity in Cw721QueryMsg Fields
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721QueryMsg enum defines fields like token_id: String, owner: String, spender: String, etc. These are defined as generic String types without explicit validation or normalization. In CosmWasm/CW721 implementations, token IDs are typically expected to be non-empty strings, but the type system does not enforce this. This creates ambiguity in value representation - the same logical token ID could be represented as different string values (e.g., 'token123' vs ' token123' with leading space) that would compare equal semantically but have different bit representations. If equality operations compare raw string bytes without normalization, these equivalent values would compare as unequal.
vulnerabilities.location: Cw721QueryMsg enum fields (token_id, owner, spender, etc.), lines 10-100+

vulnerabilities.title: Missing State Commitment Timing for Query Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721QueryMsg enum defines multiple query operations (OwnerOf, Approval, Approvals, Operator, etc.) but lacks explicit state commitment timing semantics. In CosmWasm, query operations should be idempotent and not modify state, but the current definition doesn't prevent stateful implementations. If a query operation modifies state (e.g., increments counters, logs access), and the state is committed before operation verification, this creates a timing vulnerability. An attacker could craft queries that appear to succeed but leave state in an inconsistent condition.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Interface Definition Compatibility for External Protocol Integration
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721QueryMsg enum defines query messages for a CW721 (CosmWasm NFT) implementation, but lacks explicit interface definition compatibility with external protocols. The enum defines query operations but doesn't specify parameter counts, struct field completeness, or function name compatibility with external NFT protocols. This creates ABI encoding mismatches when integrating with external NFT protocols. For example, if the external protocol expects 6 parameters but the interface declares 5, or if the Route struct is missing required fields like factory address, encoding/decoding fails.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in Query Functions
vulnerabilities.description: The query functions in this file (OwnerOf, Approval, Approvals, Operator, AllOperators, Tokens, AllTokens) do not provide users with mechanisms to specify acceptable execution bounds or minimum acceptable outputs. While these are query functions (view calls), the lack of user control parameters means users cannot express their acceptable outcomes, making them vulnerable to MEV extraction or front-running attacks where malicious actors can manipulate the execution environment to extract value from users.
vulnerabilities.location: All query functions in the Cw721QueryMsg enum

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Critical Execute Functions in Cw721Execute Interface
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Execute trait defines 10 critical execute functions (transfer_nft, send_nft, approve, revoke, approve_all, revoke_all, burn) but provides no access control mechanisms. These functions modify state, transfer assets, or change permissions without any access restrictions. In the context of a CW721 (CosmWasm NFT standard), these functions are typically only meant to be callable by the NFT owner or authorized operators, but the interface provides no way to enforce this. This is a critical vulnerability because it allows any actor to perform these operations on any NFT, leading to complete loss of asset control.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization in Cw721Execute Trait Methods
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Execute trait defines execute methods (transfer_nft, send_nft, approve, etc.) but lacks explicit authorization checks in the trait definition. Implementations must verify caller authorization before executing state-changing operations. Without proper authorization, any caller could execute privileged operations.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization in Cw721Query Trait Methods
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Query trait defines query methods (owner_of, operator, approvals, etc.) but lacks explicit authorization checks in the trait definition. While query methods typically don't change state, some implementations may perform state changes in query methods (e.g., for gas refunds, rebates). Without authorization checks, attackers could trigger unauthorized state changes through query methods.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Context Binding in Signature-Based Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Execute trait defines multiple authorization-sensitive operations (transfer_nft, send_nft, burn, approve, revoke, approve_all, revoke_all) but provides no mechanism to bind the intended executor or execution context to the authorization. This allows front-runners to submit operations with hostile contexts, consuming nonces/signatures before the intended user can execute.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in Call Function
vulnerabilities.description: The `call` function in `Cw721Contract` executes arbitrary messages without allowing users to specify minimum acceptable outputs or execution bounds. This exposes users to unfavorable execution outcomes when operations can be partially completed or manipulated.

vulnerabilities.title: Validation Timing Issue in Call Function
vulnerabilities.description: The `call` function executes WasmMsg::Execute without validating the message content before execution. If the message is malformed or invalid, the execution could complete with invalid state changes before any validation occurs.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control in Interface
vulnerabilities.description: The `Cw721Contract` interface declares critical functions like `call` without access control indicators. Functions that execute arbitrary messages should indicate restrictions but none are present in the interface declaration.

vulnerabilities.title: Return Value Unit Mismatch in tokens Function
vulnerabilities.description: The `tokens` function returns `StdResult<TokensResponse>` but the caller may expect a different unit structure. When the caller uses this return value in calculations, the unit mismatch causes incorrect accounting.

vulnerabilities.title: Return Value Unit Mismatch in all_tokens Function
vulnerabilities.description: The `all_tokens` function returns `StdResult<TokensResponse>` but the caller may expect a different unit structure. When the caller uses this return value in calculations, the unit mismatch causes incorrect accounting.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on `call` Function Allows Unauthorized Contract Interaction
vulnerabilities.description: The `call` function in the `Cw721Contract` struct performs a critical operation: it executes messages to a CW721 contract. This function has no access control restrictions, allowing any entity to invoke it. Since this function directly interacts with external contracts and can trigger state changes, it requires access control to prevent unauthorized operations.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Caller Verification in Automatic Handlers
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Contract helper struct provides query and execution methods but lacks any caller verification in its call() method. While this file itself doesn't contain automatic currency handlers, the vulnerability pattern emerges when this contract is used in broader context where the contract receives native tokens without verification.

vulnerabilities.title: Authorization Context Binding Missing in Signature Verification
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Contract implementation lacks proper binding of authorization context (executor, parameters) in signature verification. The `call` method accepts any `ExecuteMsg<T, E>` without verifying that the caller is authorized or that the message parameters match the intended authorization. This allows front-running attacks where an attacker can intercept an authorization and submit it with hostile parameters.
vulnerabilities.location: impl<Q: CustomMsg, E: CustomMsg> Cw721Contract<Q, E> call

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Cw721ExecuteMsg Variants
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721ExecuteMsg enum defines multiple execute variants (TransferNft, SendNft, Approve, Revoke, ApproveAll, RevokeAll, Burn) that are intended to be dispatched by a contract's execute handler. However, this enum itself is marked with #[cw_serde], meaning it is intended for serialization/deserialization and will be used in messages sent to the contract. Since these variants perform critical operations (transfers, approvals, burns), they must be protected by access control in the execute handler. Without proper access control, any external actor can invoke these functions, leading to unauthorized transfers, approvals, and burns.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on NFT Minting and State Initialization Functions
vulnerabilities.description: The trait interface defines multiple execute functions (e.g., `transfer_nft`, `send_nft`, `approve`, `revoke`, `approve_all`, `revoke_all`, `burn`) but lacks any access control on state-modifying operations. In particular, functions that initialize or update critical economic state (e.g., ownership, approvals, rental terms, token existence) are publicly callable without authorization, enabling front-running, state manipulation, and fee avoidance.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Approve/ApproveAll Functions Enables Allowance Manipulation
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721ExecuteMsg enum defines Approve and ApproveAll operations, but the file contains only the message definition, not the implementation. However, in typical cw721 implementations, these functions update state (allowance mappings) that are used in economic calculations (e.g., transfer permissions, fees, rewards). Without proper access control (e.g., `only_owner` or `can_approve` checks), any user can manipulate these allowances at critical times.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Check in ApproveAll and Approve Operations
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721ExecuteMsg enum defines Approve and ApproveAll operations that allow operators to manage tokens on behalf of owners. However, the message definition itself does not include any authorization verification. In a secure implementation, these operations should verify that the caller is either the token owner or an authorized operator. Without this check, any actor could approve themselves or others to manage tokens, leading to unauthorized token transfers.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Context Binding in Approve/ApproveAll Messages
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721ExecuteMsg enum defines Approve and ApproveAll messages that allow operators to manage allowances, but these messages lack binding of the token owner's address in the authorization context. This allows front-running attacks where an attacker can submit the same authorization with a different token ID or spender, consuming the allowance without the owner's intent.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on `into_cosmos_msg` Allows Unauthorized Message Construction
vulnerabilities.description: The `into_cosmos_msg` method in `Cw721ReceiveMsg` constructs a `WasmMsg::Execute` without verifying the caller's authorization. Since this function is public and not restricted by any access control modifiers, any external actor can construct arbitrary `Execute` messages targeting any contract address. This enables attackers to construct malicious messages that could be used in replay attacks, front-running, or to bypass intended receiver-side validation logic.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Input Validation on `token_id` and `sender` Fields Enables Invalid Message Construction
vulnerabilities.description: The `Cw721ReceiveMsg` struct accepts `sender: String` and `token_id: String` fields without validation. Since `into_cosmos_msg` directly serializes these fields into a `WasmMsg::Execute`, an attacker can construct messages with invalid addresses (e.g., malformed Bech32 strings, empty strings, or excessively long strings). This can cause downstream receivers to revert unexpectedly or behave incorrectly when processing these messages. The lack of validation also enables denial-of-service via message bloat or injection attacks.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Error Handling on `into_binary` Failure Leaves Message Construction Incomplete
vulnerabilities.description: The `into_cosmos_msg` function calls `self.into_binary()?`, which may fail if serialization fails. However, the function does not handle this failure explicitly, and the `?` operator propagates the error. While this prevents message construction on failure, it does not provide context about why the failure occurred. More critically, if `into_binary` fails after partial state mutation (e.g., if this were a stateful operation), the caller would receive an error but no message, leaving the operation in an ambiguous state. In a stateful context, this could lead to inconsistent accounting if the caller assumes the message was constructed successfully.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Cw721Receiver Interface
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Receiver interface declares the receive_nft function without any access control restrictions. This allows any external actor to invoke the function and manipulate state or trigger logic that should be restricted to authorized entities.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on State-Modifying Functions in Cw721Contract
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721Contract struct implements several functions that query external state but lack access control. While the provided code shows only query functions, the pattern reveals a critical access control boundary violation: functions that read and return state used in economic calculations (e.g., token balances, operator approvals, ownership) are publicly callable without any access restrictions. This enables front-running, MEV extraction, and timing-based manipulation of state-dependent operations.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Receiver Implementation for CW721 NFT Receiver Pattern
vulnerabilities.description: The provided code defines data structures for CW721 NFT receive messages but does not implement the required CW721 receiver interface. This means contracts attempting to receive CW721 tokens will not properly handle incoming tokens, potentially causing permanent token loss.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Context Binding in Cw721ReceiverMsg
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721ReceiveMsg struct lacks binding of the intended recipient address in its serialization. This allows any actor can forge receive messages for arbitrary token IDs and senders, bypassing the Cw721 standard's authorization requirements.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Mint Function
vulnerabilities.description: The contract's Mint function lacks access control, allowing any user to mint new tokens without authorization. This is a critical vulnerability as it enables unlimited token inflation and potential token devaluation.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in Approve/ApproveAll Functions
vulnerabilities.description: The Approve and ApproveAll functions allow operators to transfer or spend tokens on behalf of the owner without requiring the owner to specify minimum acceptable outputs or execution bounds. This exposes owners to unfavorable execution where operators could transfer more value than intended or at inopportune times.
vulnerabilities.location: Approve and ApproveAll functions in Cw721ExecuteMsg enum

vulnerabilities.title: Missing User Protection in Transfer Function
vulnerabilities.description: The TransferNft function does not provide users with mechanisms to specify minimum acceptable outputs or execution bounds. When users request token transfers, they cannot protect against unfavorable execution conditions, exposing them to potential loss of value due to market manipulation or adversarial actions.

vulnerabilities.title: Validation Timing Issue in Mint Function
vulnerabilities.description: The Mint function executes token creation before validating that the token ID is unique and the minter has sufficient authority. This allows invalid operations to complete, potentially leading to token inflation or unauthorized minting.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on Mint Function Enables Fee Evasion via Timing Manipulation
vulnerabilities.description: The contract's Mint function lacks access control, allowing any user to mint tokens at arbitrary times. This enables front-running of admin operations and manipulation of state used in economic calculations. Specifically, if the contract implements fee calculations based on time of day, block timestamps, or other time-dependent variables, users can time their mint operations to avoid fees or gain unfair advantages.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control in Minter Management
vulnerabilities.description: The contract implements a CW721 NFT minter pattern but lacks proper access control on minter management functions. The `Minter` query response shows the minter is set to admin, but there's no verification that only the minter can mint tokens. An attacker could potentially call mint functions directly if the minter address is compromised or if the minter is set to a predictable address.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Burn Authorization Check in Burn Execute Handler
vulnerabilities.description: The Burn execute handler in the CW721 contract does not verify that the caller is authorized to burn the NFT. This allows any actor to burn arbitrary tokens, destroying value without authorization.
vulnerabilities.location: ExecuteMsg::Burn handler (likely in execute.rs or entry.rs)

vulnerabilities.title: Missing cw2 Contract Version Initialization Guard
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function does not verify that cw2 contract version is not already set before calling cw2::set_contract_version. This allows re-initialization of an already instantiated contract, potentially corrupting state and enabling replay attacks.

vulnerabilities.title: Incorrect cw2::set_contract_version Return Value Ignored
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function calls cw2::set_contract_version but ignores its return value. If set_contract_version fails (e.g., due to storage corruption or re-initialization), the error is silently swallowed, leaving the contract in an undefined state.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing cw2::set_contract_version Parameter Validation
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function calls cw2::set_contract_version(deps.storage, CONTRACT_NAME, CONTRACT_VERSION) without validating that CONTRACT_NAME and CONTRACT_VERSION are non-empty or valid semver strings. If these constants are misconfigured (e.g., empty string, invalid semver), the function proceeds and corrupts state.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing cw2::set_contract_version Storage Corruption Risk
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function calls cw2::set_contract_version(deps.storage, CONTRACT_NAME, CONTRACT_VERSION) without verifying that deps.storage is valid or initialized. If deps.storage is corrupted or uninitialized, the function proceeds and corrupts state.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing cw2::set_contract_version Reentrancy Protection
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function calls cw2::set_contract_version(deps.storage, CONTRACT_NAME, CONTRACT_VERSION) without implementing reentrancy protection. If cw2::set_contract_version internally calls back into the contract (e.g., via callbacks or hooks), the function proceeds and corrupts state.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Access Control on State-Modifying Functions in Cw721 Receiver
vulnerabilities.description: The Cw721 receiver implementation exposes functions that modify state without access control, enabling users to manipulate timing of state updates before admin operations. Specifically, the `into_cosmos_msg` function constructs a WasmMsg that may be used to call arbitrary contracts, but there is no verification that the target contract is authorized to receive NFTs.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing cw2 Contract Version Initialization Check in Instantiate
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function calls cw2::set_contract_version but does not verify the current contract version before proceeding. This can lead to re-initialization of an already initialized contract, potentially bypassing version-specific migration logic or allowing state corruption if the contract is re-initialized with different parameters.

vulnerabilities.title: Incorrect cw721 Contract Initialization Without Proper State Isolation
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function creates a new Cw721Contract instance using .default() and calls .instantiate() on it. However, this does not ensure proper state isolation between contract versions or migrations. If the contract is re-initialized, the previous state may persist, leading to double-initialization or version mismatch issues.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing cw2 Version Verification Before cw721 Initialization
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function calls cw2::set_contract_version but does not verify the current contract version before proceeding. This can lead to re-initialization of an already initialized contract, potentially bypassing version-specific migration logic or allowing state corruption if the contract is re-initialized with different parameters.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing cw2 Contract Version Initialization in Instantiate
vulnerabilities.description: The instantiate function calls cw2::set_contract_version but does not verify the current contract version matches EXPECTED_FROM_VERSION. This allows instantiation with any version, potentially causing migration issues.
